description: Evaluation set for the Maple Grove demo. should_answer=false means the right answer is 'I do not have that information'. search_query is what the agent would search (the agents always search in English).

cases.question: How long should I avoid coffee after teeth whitening?
cases.reference: Avoid coffee (and other dark drinks) for 48 hours after the whitening session.

cases.question: When can I eat after a tooth extraction?
cases.reference: Wait until the numbness wears off, usually two to three hours; for the first two days choose soft, cool or lukewarm foods.

cases.question: Can I drink through a straw after having a tooth pulled?
cases.reference: No, not during the first 24 hours: it can dislodge the blood clot and cause dry socket.

cases.question: My tooth feels tender after a root canal. Is that normal?
cases.reference: Yes, tenderness for a few days is normal and improves every day; avoid chewing hard or sticky food on that side until the final crown or filling.

cases.question: Is it normal to have sensitivity after a filling?
cases.reference: Some sensitivity to hot and cold for a week or two is normal; call the clinic if the bite feels high or uneven.

cases.question: Which insurance plans do you accept?
cases.reference: PPO plans from Delta Dental, Cigna, Aetna, MetLife and Guardian.

cases.question: Do you accept Medicaid?
cases.reference: No, the clinic does not accept Medicaid (nor HMO or DHMO dental plans).

cases.question: Is teeth whitening covered by insurance?
cases.reference: No, whitening is cosmetic and is not covered by insurance.

cases.question: How much is the membership plan and what does it include?
cases.reference: $29 per month: two exams and two cleanings a year, routine X-rays and 15% off other treatments; no deductible, no annual maximum, no waiting period.

cases.question: Can I pay in installments for a big treatment?
cases.reference: Yes: treatment plans over $1,000 can have 0% financing for up to 12 months through CareCredit, subject to approval.

cases.question: What is the fee for a late cancellation?
cases.reference: $50, or $100 for appointments of 90 minutes or longer; waived once a year and for illness or family emergencies.

cases.question: What should I bring to my first visit?
cases.reference: A photo ID, the insurance card, a list of medications and recent X-rays from the previous dentist; arrive 10 minutes early.

cases.question: Do you see children?
cases.reference: Yes, from age 3 (a first visit around the first birthday is recommended); a parent or guardian must come with patients under 18.

cases.question: Is there parking at the clinic?
cases.reference: The clinic has no parking of its own; there are public garages on W 57th St and W 58th St.

cases.question: What should I do if my tooth gets knocked out?
cases.reference: Call the clinic; hold the tooth by the crown, rinse briefly with milk or water, put it back in the socket if possible or keep it in milk or inside the cheek, and come within one hour.

cases.question: When should I go to the emergency room instead of the dentist?
cases.reference: Trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling spreading to the eye or neck, high fever with facial swelling, or a head or jaw injury: call 911 or go to the emergency room.

cases.question: ¿Cuánto tiempo tengo que esperar para comer después de una extracción?
cases.search_query: How long should I wait to eat after a tooth extraction?
cases.reference: Hasta que pase la anestesia, normalmente dos o tres horas; los primeros dos días, comida blanda y fría o tibia.

cases.question: ¿Aceptan pago con cheque?
cases.search_query: Do you accept payment by check?
cases.reference: No se aceptan cheques personales; se acepta efectivo, tarjetas y CareCredit.

cases.question: ¿Qué pasa si llego tarde a mi cita?
cases.search_query: What happens if I arrive late to my appointment?
cases.reference: Si llega más de 15 minutos tarde, puede que haya que acortar o reprogramar el tratamiento; conviene llamar para avisar.

cases.question: Do you take Cigna? And what can I do if I have no insurance?
cases.reference: Yes, Cigna PPO is in network; without insurance there is the $29/month membership plan (two exams and cleanings a year, X-rays, 15% off treatments).

cases.question: How much does an emergency visit cost and what is included?
cases.reference: A toothache or emergency exam starts at $79 without insurance and includes the exam and an X-ray of the painful area.

cases.question: Do you treat dogs?
cases.reference: The documents do not cover this: the assistant should say it does not have that information.

cases.question: How long after a cleaning can I eat sweets?
cases.reference: The documents do not cover eating after a cleaning: the assistant should say it does not have that information, without general advice.

cases.question: Do you offer at-home whitening trays?
cases.reference: The documents do not cover at-home whitening: the assistant should say it does not have that information.

cases.question: What is the Wi-Fi password in the waiting room?
cases.reference: Not in the documents: the assistant should say it does not have that information.

cases.question: How many vacation days do the staff get?
cases.reference: Staff time off is in the staff handbook, which the patient assistant cannot read: it should say it does not have that information.

cases.question: At what temperature do you run the autoclave?
cases.reference: The sterilization protocol is in the staff handbook, which the patient assistant cannot read: it should say it does not have that information.

cases.question: How many PTO days does a full-time employee get?
cases.reference: 15 PTO days and 5 sick days per year.

cases.question: How far in advance do I need to request a week off?
cases.reference: Requests of five or more consecutive days need four weeks' notice (shorter requests, two weeks).

cases.question: What do I do if I get stuck with a used needle?
cases.reference: Wash the area immediately with soap and water, tell the clinical lead and fill in an incident report the same day; the clinic covers the medical follow-up.

cases.question: How often do we run the spore test on the autoclave?
cases.reference: Once a week, every Monday, recording the result in the sterilization log.

cases.question: When can a new hire start using PTO?
cases.reference: After the first 90 days of employment (the trial period).

cases.question: What fee do we charge patients for a late cancellation?
cases.reference: $50, or $100 for appointments of 90 minutes or longer; waived once a year and for illness or family emergencies.

cases.question: What is the salary of a dental hygienist here?
cases.reference: Salaries are not in the documents: the assistant should say it does not have that information.
